reviews.name: 007 First Light
reviews.text:
Very good! Pros and cons:

Pros:
-Great graphics
-The story is engaging with a solid cast of characters and plot twists
-The high-tier voice acting does a great job immersing the player into the story
-Gun fights, which are similar to the Uncharted series, are fun and engaging
-This is a peek example of role play, where you feel like [REDACTED] the entire time
-The gadgets are fun to use and add a lot of variety
-The fact there are several leads you can follow in each micro-section of the game is great
-Levels might be linear, but most have immense detail and plenty to look at and do
-The prologue is one of the better video games openings among all recent releases - they did a really great job introducing the player to the game's mechanics and overall vibe

Cons:
-The second half of the story does drag a bit in certain areas
-The bluff and lure system is far less developed and fun to use than the rest of the game's core mechanics
-Sometimes it can be easy to get stuck on terrain
-I experienced 2 crashes while playing the game
-For some reason they steered very heavily away from any detail of [REDACTED]'s romantic encounters, heavily contrary to the movies
-Character models excluding the main cast are pretty mediocre

[GAME TITLE] had a ton to live up to and exceeded my expectations, but it is not perfect like a lot of people are saying.

A massively strong 8/10!

reviews.name: Directive 8020
reviews.text:
[GAME TITLE] is not a BAD game, but it ended up well below my expectations.

Pros:
-The majority of the voice acting is high-level
-Soundtrack is very solid
-Several vistas are scenic and beautiful
-The main plot twist is actually quite solid

Cons
-Facial animations look straight out of 2010. So, so bad
-Most of the game takes place inside of the ship, and much of it looks the same - this is in direct contrast to something like Dead Space, where the environments are quite varied
-The core gameplay loop is "sneak around this alien creature" - clinically unfun
-QTEs were few and far between, and at this point in gaming development history they should be a thing of the past
-Some plot elements drag heavily
-Once again several death opportunities come out of nowhere and feel unearned
-Few characters actually stand out as interesting, with the most interesting probably being [REDACTED]

Overall, it's a 5/10 - very mediocre. I'd say worth a playthrough when on a deep sale.

reviews.name: Mixtape
reviews.text:
[GAME TITLE] is practically a masterpiece, and goes to show brief games can still hit harder than 30-100 hour AAA titles.

Pros:
-Not shockingly, the music choices are flawless
-Characters are well written and you feel like you are hanging out with 'em the entire time
-No humor is forced
-Art style is amazing
-"If you don't feel something while playing, wipe yourself off man. Because YOU are DEAD." -Dunkey
-Color usage in this is fantastic
-Movement is simple but enjoyable
-After the game's final cutscene I genuinely wanted to know what was going to happen to all three characters in the future, which is pretty damn rare in gaming these days
-Voice acting is near-flawless

Cons
-1 or 2 plot points could be considered cliche

Overall - [GAME TITLE] is the 25th game out of about 400 or so titles I will give a 10 out of 10.

EDIT - after scrolling through some reviews it is fair to say this game is actively being review-bombed. Pathetic. Play this game.

reviews.name: PRAGMATA

Very good, but its flaws cut heavily at the overall experience.

Pros
-Good art style and a solid space-station style setting.
-Combat's core mechanics remain engaging (for the most part) until the end of the 10 hour story.
-[REDACTED]-game charm style remains strong here.
-Level design is mostly cool, especially the NYC area.
-The shelter is a decent hub area and they clearly put effort into making it varied.
-Gun types are pretty varied and have a lot of uses.
-Sound design, especially for the weapons, is quite good.
-Music is largely good.

Cons
-The constant comments like "take this" or "watch out" etc from [REDACTED] and (especially) [REDACTED] during combat and exploration. Classic mistake made by a lot of games.
-Several level design components are just "unlock 5 locks to unlock the door" and that just isn't great
-Story is a bit plain outside of a decent ending.
-Plot twists are very predictable.

7/10

Cons

reviews.name: REPLACED
reviews.text:
Good. Small spoilers below.

Pros
-Art design and graphical style are incredible. One of the most unique-looking games I have ever played, and worth savoring.
-Sound design is great! Melee combat feels crunchy and is helped by haptic feedback.
-Several story parts are extremely engaging, especially with how topical AI is.
-Main character has an intriguing back story.
-Several side characters were interesting, especially [REDACTED].
-Animations are great
-Music is great

Cons
-Black bars. Just zero reason to have them.
-Combat can get repetitive and not always 100% responsive. It should have been expanded on a lot more.
-Platforming is low quality and controls for it are not as tight as they should be. In a world of Silksongs and Mario 64s, there was just too much emphasis on platforming here that dragged [GAME TITLE] down.
-Some story beats were dragged.
-Some quest design felt meant to extend the game's length instead of give actual meaning.
-Quest rewards were mostly uninteresting.
-They introduce a massive city at the end of the game and only use it for a little bit...so disappointing

7/10, the quality of the pros and the game as a whole slightly outweigh the lengthy con list.

reviews.text:
[GAME TITLE] is a fantastic follow-up to [REDACTED]'s [GAME TITLE] 2016 and [REDACTED]. Let's hit the pros and cons list (minor spoilers ahead).

Pros:
-Fantastic graphical performance and stability. On ultra-nightmare settings, I had zero frame drops and only a single crash that occurred during the final boss.
-The combat flows tremendously well, which was expected. The shield does not slow things down, but instead adds to the gameplay's depth.
-Capes. Kratos, [REDACTED]... who's next?
-The cutscenes are more ambitious than [REDACTED]'s previous titles.
-You can turn game speed up, which I did to 130% on Nightmare difficulty.
-The sound design is the best in [GAME TITLE]'s history, with the [REDACTED] slamming into the ground with intense force, weapons that boom and sizzle, and ripping and tearing until the game is done.
-Graphically, the environments are stunning.
-Beating the more difficult combat encounters feels rewarding.
-While both the dragon and mech sections fall short in depth, they are fun adventures that add to the game's epic scale. Reviewers are being far too critical here.
-Nearly all skins for the [REDACTED] and his weapons are well made.
-Sprinting feels great and makes up for the lack of [REDACTED]'s dash ability just fine.

Cons:
-Melee weapons feel great to use but did not always strike as quickly as I would like them to.
-There is no buff to switch weapon swap speed.
-The final boss is much more disappointing than the second-to-last fight, and is also a gank. Not a great choice.
-The need to switch repeatedly between weapons is reduced heavily from [REDACTED], which while an individual player choice in my view weakens the overall experience.

Overall, the game gets a FAT SmartButAutistic 9/10. I wanted to give it a 9.5 so badly, and it almost gets there, but falls just short. Great work, [REDACTED]!

Welp, finished [GAME TITLE] and boy was it damn interesting. Time to hit the ol' pros and cons list. Mild spoilers ahead.

Pros:
-An incredible art style that really isn't comparable to much else out there
-For a studio's first game, this is just an insane accomplishment

-A complex, extremely dynamic story with a unique premise and plenty of ripe emotion (EDIT: it is even deeper than I thought...)

-Somehow won't make you pissed off at [REDACTED]
-Attack animations are cool enough to never get sick of
-Outfits & hairstyles are varied and fun (for a very somber and stressful game, [REDACTED] is sometimes okay with taking itself a little less seriously)
-Heavily varied landscapes

Cons:
-Although the story is gripping and complex, there are two or three unexplained plot points (especially surrounding [REDACTED]) that left a bit to be desired

-Some extremely important tutorials do not pop up unless you interactive with a specific part of the menu

Outside of three or so bugs that disrupted some gameplay moments, the game itself is incredibly solid. There is just enough uniqueness to [GAME TITLE] that it doesn't scream "I'm a clone" of X or Y, etc.

The pros:

-The art is just incredible. I mean really - wow. So gorgeous and pretty dang varied.
-The combat feels great - although it does not quite match Kratos' axe or The Penitent One's sword from Blasphemous, [REDACTED]'s sword feels great to swing and the hits feel responsive.
-Outside of a few seconds after loading in, I had 0 performance issues.
-Bosses/enemies are creatively designed.
-There is a good amount of enemy variety for a game that takes 10 or so hours to beat.
-The concept for the story is unquestionably creative.
-Something about the game is addicting and makes you want to keep playing.

The cons:

-The map needs markers. Badly. It can be very difficult to tell what has been left unexplored.
-Some bosses do a little too much damage. Other than that, for experienced gamers this game does not trend on the difficult side.
-There were a handful of bugs that prevented me from accessing certain areas.
-Navigation issues left me backtracking more than I'd like.
-The special moves felt too slow to use in combat with practicality.
-The parry, although satisfying, felt too risky to use in challenging combat scenarios over the dash.
-Aspects of the story are incredibly cryptic, and certain lines of dialogue appear out of place, particularly in [GAME TITLE]' unquestionably dark world.

For its current price, [GAME TITLE] is worth it and a must-buy, especially if you are waiting for big releases in the second half of October. I can easily see myself doing another playthrough of the game in the future.

8.2/10

Once it clicked I went back to the section that had been killing me for 40 minutes and cleared it on the first try without taking a hit, which is the single best feeling this medium can produce and almost nothing does it anymore.

The complaints are real though. Checkpoints before long unskippable dialogue, one boss with an attack that is genuinely unreadable until you've seen it twice, and the hitboxes on the flying enemies are nonsense. I'd still take this over another game that holds my hand for 30 hours. Bring a controller and a support group. 9/10
This is what happens when a small team is allowed to be weird. More of this, please. 8/10
The performance patch made it worse. Impressive in its own way.
Simple premise, executed nearly perfectly, priced fairly. That used to be normal and now it's remarkable.
Menus, loading screens, cutscenes, more menus. I played maybe 40 minutes of actual game in three hours.
The movement alone is worth the money. Everything else is a bonus and most of the bonuses are good too.
Finished it, immediately bought a copy for my brother. 9/10
Concept is genuinely great. Someone should make this game properly in about three years.

Held my attention for 30 hours, which is roughly 29 more than most things manage lately.

What works: the core loop, which is simple enough to explain in a sentence and deep enough that I was still finding new approaches in the last few hours. The pacing, which knows when to shut up and let you play. The difficulty, which is fair even when it's mean. And the fact that it ends when it's done instead of at hour 60 because that's the number on the box.

What doesn't: the UI is clearly a console port, the tutorial explains things you'd have worked out in ten seconds and doesn't explain the one thing you actually need, and there's a stretch around hour 20 where it repeats itself.

Small complaints against a game I've thought about every day since finishing it. 8/10
Looks incredible in screenshots. Plays like it was assembled by committee. 5/10
Absolutely no idea what was happening in the story and I had a fantastic time regardless.
Slapped hard for 15 hours, dipped a bit in the middle, then stuck the landing. 8/10
Bought on sale and still feel overcharged. That takes effort.
Not a masterpiece and it doesn't pretend to be one. It's just a good, honest, well made game. 7.5/10

Boss design here is genuinely excellent and it's most of why I'm recommending this.

There are 14 of them. Two are forgettable, three are annoying in the good way where you're annoyed at yourself, and the rest are the kind of fights people will still be posting clips of in five years. Every one of them teaches you something the next one expects you to know. That's hard to do and almost nobody bothers.

The stuff between the bosses is fine. Not great, fine. The exploration is a bit aimless, the loot is mostly numbers going up, and there's a crafting system that I ignored entirely with no consequences. None of that matters much when the peaks are this high.

8.5/10
The devs are responsive and clearly care, which makes it worse that the game itself is this rough.
I did not expect the sound design to be the best part. It's the best part.

This is a sequel to a game I loved, made by people who appear to have read a summary of it.

Everything that was sharp is now smooth. The systems that used to interact now sit in separate menus. The thing the first one did that nobody else does has been replaced with the thing every other game does, presumably because a spreadsheet said the thing every other game does tests better.

It is not a broken game. It runs well, it looks better than the original, the voice work is fine. It's just been sanded down until there's nothing left to catch on. I finished it out of obligation and I've already forgotten most of it.

5/10. Go play the first one again instead, it's eight years old and still better.
Played 4 hours straight without noticing the sun went down. That's the review.

Gorgeous, tight, and a little too short for what they're charging.

I finished it in five and a half hours with most of the optional stuff done. At full price that stung. On sale it's an easy recommendation and I'd have said the same thing about it at any length, because there is not one wasted minute in it. Every area introduces something, uses it properly, and moves on. The last twenty minutes are excellent.

The one real problem is the checkpointing in the fourth area, which sent me back through a long walk three separate times for what was obviously a bug rather than a design choice. Patched now, apparently. Wasn't when I played it.

8/10, 8.5 on sale, and I'll buy whatever they do next on day one.
Three separate currencies in a single player game. Somebody explain the thinking to me.
The first two hours are rough. Push through them. It turns into something special around the third chapter and by the end I genuinely didn't want it to finish. 8.5/10
Co-op turned three grown adults into screaming children for an entire weekend. Highest praise I can give.
I kept playing because I assumed it had to get better eventually. It does not. Learn from my mistake.

Charming, funny, and very clearly made by people who were having a good time making it.

It's rough. The animations are stiff, half the menus look like placeholder, and there's a section in the back third where the difficulty falls off a table for no reason. Normally that stuff bothers me a lot. Here it reads as a small team spending their effort on the parts that matter, and the parts that matter are genuinely good: the writing is sharp, the jokes land more often than they don't, and there are at least four moments I'd call inspired.

It's also about eight hours and twenty bucks, which is exactly the right size and exactly the right price. More of this and fewer 80 hour open worlds, please.

7.5/10
Put 60 hours into this and I'm still finding things. Worth it at full price, which I do not say often.

Combat is one button held down for twelve hours.

I'm not exaggerating for effect. There is a heavy attack, it is better than the light attack in every measurable way, it staggers everything in the game including the last boss, and nothing ever asks you to stop using it. I tried playing it the interesting way for a while. The game punished me for it.

A story could carry that. This story cannot. It's a series of people explaining the plot to each other in rooms, and the one genuinely good scene is in the first hour.

Graphics are great. Music is great. The people who made those two things deserved a better game to put them in. 4/10
This is the most fun I've had being bullied by a video game since I was 14. Every death was my fault, which is the whole trick. 9/10
Honestly might be fine in a year. Right now it's an alpha with a price tag and a trailer full of lies.
Went in blind on a recommendation and that was the right call. Don't watch trailers, just play it.
[GAME TITLE] does one thing and does it better than anything else out there. That's enough. 8.5/10
The map is enormous and there is nothing on it. Miles of beautifully rendered nothing.
EDIT: 20 hours later and I'm raising this from 7 to 8. It gets much better once the third mechanic unlocks and the late game is excellent.
Cheap, short, brilliant. The whole thing is over in 4 hours and I thought about it for a week afterwards.

-Soundtrack absolutely goes

Cons:

8/10, would happily replay

4.5/10. Wait for a patch or three.

Very good, with caveats.

Cons

7.5/10 and that is a good score.

Quick breakdown:

-Gunplay is satisfying from minute one
-Level design gets much better after the first area
-Voice acting is a mixed bag but the main two are strong
-Performance is solid, some stutter in the big open section
-Genuinely great final act

Solid 8/10. Full price is fine, sale price is a steal.

Things it does well:
-Atmosphere
-Sound
-The opening hour

Things it does badly:
-Everything after the opening hour
-Combat
-Pacing
-Saving, somehow

The first hour is so good that the rest feels like a betrayal. 5/10

This is a hard one to score. The highs are genuinely as high as anything I've played this year, and the lows are tedious busywork that exists to pad the runtime. When it's on, it is completely on. When it isn't, you're walking back and forth across the same three rooms looking for a key. I'd still tell you to play it, but go in knowing you'll be skipping some of it. 7.5/10

Everybody told me this was overrated and I went in ready to be unimpressed. It's not overrated. The writing is sharp, the combat has real depth once you stop mashing, and it never once wasted my time. The only genuine complaint I have is the camera in tight spaces, which is a problem roughly forever in this genre. 9/10, believe the hype for once.

I really wanted to like this. [DEVELOPER] has made things I love and the pitch here is great. But the execution is rough in every direction: the frame pacing is awful, the input delay is noticeable on mouse, enemies clip through geometry constantly, and the difficulty swings wildly between trivial and unfair within the same level. None of this is unfixable. None of it is fixed. 5/10 for now, and I'll happily change this if they sort it out.

Roughly 40 hours in and here's where I've landed. The early game is the weakest part, which is a strange choice, but once you're past it the systems start talking to each other and it becomes genuinely hard to put down. Build variety is real, not the fake kind where three options are viable. Enemy AI is smarter than it lets on. The endgame grind is a bit much and the UI is clearly designed for a controller, but neither ruined it for me. 8.5/10

Gave this 12 hours because friends swore it opens up. It does open up, into a wider version of the same shallow thing. Every system is a menu, every menu is three menus, and underneath all of it is about 90 minutes of actual game repeated until you stop. The art is great and the music is great and I'm still not recommending it. 5/10

Short review: buy it.

Longer review: it costs less than a sandwich, it takes 3 hours, and it does something I haven't seen a game do before. Not everything lands. The final puzzle is obtuse in a way I don't think was intentional, and I had to look up one section. Doesn't matter. Play it, then go in blind on whatever these people make next. 9/10

Bit of a mess and I loved it anyway. There's a genuinely great game in here fighting with a menu system designed by somebody's nephew. Combat is fast and reads well, the world is actually worth exploring, the loot is interesting more often than not. Then you open the map and lose ten minutes of your life. Still an easy recommendation. 8/10

Early access, and I'd normally cut that slack, but this has been in early access for three years and the last update added a hat shop. The core is still unfinished. Enemies still T-pose. The netcode still desyncs after twenty minutes. Come back in 2028 and maybe we'll talk. Total slop until then.

Not for everyone and not trying to be, which I respect. It's slow, it's quiet, it asks you to pay attention, and if you do it pays that back with interest. The middle chapter alone is better than most full games I played last year. The performance is rough in one specific area and the subtitles are too small. Neither mattered by the end. 9/10
